title: A Vow for the Promise Again
premise: Astrid Joubert built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days after his own engagement ended in a betrayal he's never fully explained, even to himself. When his family reunion threatens to expose the lie that he's 'happily settled,' he hires Elise Marchand, a sharp-tongued florist who once worked one of his weddings, to pose as his partner for a single weekend. But the performance cracks open old truths: Astrid's survival after the scandal cost him his honesty, and Elise knows more about what really happened at that ruined wedding than she's admitted. As the island festival approaches, Astrid must choose between protecting the reputation that rebuilt his business and telling the truth to the one person who sees him clearly—ending with him publicly owning his past at the festival, losing a flagship contract but gaining a real beginning with Elise.
about_author: V. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former event coordinator turned novelist who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happily-ever-afters. They write romances about people who are better at planning love than admitting to it.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He flawlessly runs a stranger's wedding while privately rehearsing excuses for the upcoming Joubert family reunion, where his mother expects him to bring a serious partner. The beat: polished competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: three years ago, Astrid's own wedding collapsed when his fiancé vanished mid-ceremony amid accusations Astrid never refuted. Present-day Astrid locks the memory box away. Beat: grief managed like inventory.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. His mother calls: the whole family will be on Belle-Île for the summer festival, and cousin Margaux's engagement announcement means everyone will compare partners. His sister Camille warns him not to come alone. Beat: cornered by love.

chapters.title: A Florist With Opinions
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. She storms into Astrid's studio over an unpaid invoice from a wedding her flowers nearly saved. Their sparring reveals she remembers him from the infamous ruined wedding—and doesn't buy his public version of it. Beat: friction with recognition underneath.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Astrid proposes the fake-date arrangement: one weekend, generous pay, no questions. Elise counters with her own terms, including that he answer one question of hers truthfully before it ends. Beat: a deal struck on unequal footing.

chapters.title: Packing the Performance
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He prepares Elise's briefing dossier—family tree, talking points, fabricated how-we-met—and feels sick at how easily lying has become logistics. Beat: the planner caught in his own blueprint.

chapters.title: Crossing to the Island
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. The ferry ride to Belle-Île; Elise studies the dossier, Astrid rehearses smiles. A shared joke breaks the professional surface for one unguarded moment. Beat: the mask slipping before the audience arrives.

chapters.title: First Impressions, Second Takes
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Meeting the Jouberts: warm, chaotic, observant. Grand-mère Solange sees through the performance instantly but says nothing, only squeezes Elise's hand. Beat: being seen by the wrong person first.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the welcome dinner, under pressure from Margaux's smug fiancé, Astrid takes Elise's hand without thinking—and it feels too real by dessert. Beat: the fake becomes involuntary.

chapters.title: The Question She Banked
chapters.summary: Evening walk. Elise spends her promised truthful question: 'Why did you never defend yourself?' Astrid deflects with a half-truth; she lets him, visibly filing it away. Beat: trust extended, not yet earned.

chapters.title: Margaux's Kingdom
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Margaux recruits Elise to help plan her engagement party, pulling Elise deeper into family politics and closer to secrets—including gossip about Astrid's disgraced wedding. Beat: proximity to danger disguised as favor.

chapters.title: Camille Knows
chapters.summary: Camille confronts Astrid privately: she recognizes Elise from the old wedding photos and demands to know what game he's playing. Astrid lies to the one sibling who always covered for him. Beat: loyalty strained by protection.

chapters.title: Rain on the Terrace
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Trapped indoors by a storm, Astrid and Elise share wine and almost-honesty; he describes the wedding disaster in clinical detail, omitting only his own role. Beat: intimacy built on an omission.

chapters.title: The Vendor List
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Planning Margaux's party, Elise discovers the original vendor contracts from Astrid's ruined wedding—including a payment from his then-fiancé's family that suggests a cover-up. Beat: the past resurfacing in paperwork.

chapters.title: Festival Preparations
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The town asks Astrid to consult on the annual festival—a public honor that would cement his redemption locally. His mother beams; Astrid feels the trap of reputation tightening. Beat: success as a cage.

chapters.title: An Almost Kiss
chapters.summary: After a festival committee meeting, Astrid and Elise nearly kiss on the harbor wall, interrupted by Margaux. Both retreat into their roles, shaken. Beat: desire outpacing the script.

chapters.title: Solange's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Grand-mère Solange tells Elise, obliquely, about the night of the ruined wedding—what the family saw, what they were told to believe. Beat: history told by its witness.

chapters.title: The Fiancé Returns
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Théo, the man who left him at the altar, appears on the island as Margaux's fiancé's business partner. Old panic floods back; Astrid begs Elise to stay close through the weekend. Beat: the wound walks in wearing linen.

chapters.title: Public Hand-Holding
chapters.summary: At a beach gathering, Théo greets Astrid with poisonous charm. Elise steps in, fierce and convincing, and Astrid realizes gratitude has tipped into something else. Beat: the fake date defending the real heart.

chapters.title: What Elise Found
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. She matches the contract signature to Théo's family firm: they paid to bury evidence that Théo orchestrated the scandal, letting Astrid absorb the blame. She now holds the truth Astrid never asked her to find. Beat: knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Lantern Night
chapters.summary: During the festival's lantern release, Astrid tells Elise a true thing—that he stopped believing in weddings because he stopped believing he deserved one. They kiss, finally, honestly. Beat: the turning point, tenderness achieved.

chapters.title: Morning After the Truth
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Waking beside Elise, Astrid feels terror, not joy: if she learns what he hid, the weekend collapses. He decides to control the narrative before she can. Beat: love met with management.

chapters.title: The Contract She Signed
chapters.summary: Elise finds the fine print Astrid added: a confidentiality clause covering 'all matters pertaining to prior engagements.' She realizes he planned to keep her silent even as he kissed her. Beat: romance curdling into transaction.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Elise confronts Astrid: does he want her or a witness? He insists the clause was habit, not malice; she says habit is character. She walks. Beat: the false structure fails under real weight.

chapters.title: Théo's Offer
chapters.summary: Théo corners Astrid with an offer: sign a joint statement keeping the old story intact, and Théo will steer a lucrative hotel contract to Astrid's company. Survival dressed as generosity. Beat: the price named aloud.

chapters.title: Camille's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Camille, having pieced everything together, gives Astrid a choice: tell the truth at the festival or lose her respect forever. She reveals she kept letters from the fiancé's family all along. Beat: family loyalty demanding truth.

chapters.title: The Empty Studio
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV alone. He drafts two versions of his festival speech—one safe, one true—and burns neither, unable to choose. Flashback shows the young Astrid who once believed love was worth ruin. Beat: the dark night of the planner.

chapters.title: Elise Decides
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Packing to leave the island, she rereads the contracts and realizes exposing Théo would also expose Astrid's silence. She chooses to give him until the festival's final night to speak himself. Beat: mercy with a deadline.

chapters.title: Margaux's Party
chapters.summary: The engagement party Astrid planned perfectly goes sideways when Théo toasts 'second chances' with a pointed look at Astrid. Elise, still present for the job, watches Astrid swallow it. Beat: humiliation in front of everyone he loves.

chapters.title: The Broken Centerpiece
chapters.summary: Alone after the party, Astrid destroys part of his own flawless décor—an act of rage against his own carefulness. Elise finds him among the wreckage and stays, saying nothing. Beat: collapse as beginning.

chapters.title: Confession at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Astrid tells Elise everything: that he knew Théo's family buried the truth, that he accepted silence to save his business, that the clause was fear made legal. She listens without absolution. Beat: truth offered, forgiveness pending.

chapters.title: Solange's Blessing
chapters.summary: Solange tells Astrid she has known for years and loved him anyway, and that the family's image was never worth his. She presses her late husband's watch into his hand: time to spend it. Beat: inheritance of courage.

chapters.title: Rising Action: The Leak
chapters.summary: Someone leaks the old contracts to a local journalist; the story will run during the festival. Astrid suspects Théo pre-empting him—or Camille forcing his hand. Beat: the choice being taken out of his hands.

chapters.title: The Last Briefing
chapters.summary: Astrid and Elise rebuild their alliance properly this time: no clauses, no scripts. They plan how he'll speak before the article lands. Beat: partnership replacing performance.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: The eve of the final celebration; the town glows, the journalist circles, Théo makes a last threat to ruin Astrid's business entirely if he speaks. Astrid signs nothing. Beat: stakes at maximum.

chapters.title: Climax: The Speech
chapters.summary: Before the gathered town and family, Astrid abandons his prepared remarks and tells the truth—the abandonment, the cover-up, his complicit silence. Théo storms out; the hotel contract dies; Elise watches from the crowd, unreadable. Beat: ruin chosen freely.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The fallout: clients cancel, Margaux is furious, but Camille stands beside him and Solange's quiet approval spreads through the family. Astrid feels lighter than any success ever made him. Beat: loss as liberation.

chapters.title: The Answer She Waited For
chapters.summary: Elise comes to him—not to absolve but to ask her second question: 'Who do you want to be now?' He answers plainly, and asks to start again without a contract. She agrees, on new terms. Beat: love renegotiated honestly.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Believing In
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: months later, Astrid plans one last wedding—for Camille—and hands Elise the flowers, a partnership in work and life. He believes in weddings again, cautiously, completely. Beat: vocation restored.

chapters.title: The Vow, Again
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV closing on the same harbor where they kissed. No ceremony, just two promises spoken privately: to keep choosing truth over safety. The festival lanterns rise again behind them. Beat: the vow renewed, this time real.
